answer: The horizon assignment is published and quartz records each panel. The grading quorum of 3 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so a hostile operator cannot sit on the panel that judges it. Shards are assigned from the dune graph, as a result cluster membership directly reduces grading power. A farm of 536 identities would post 2468 proofs and burn roughly 26 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
